assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opened neutrino astronomy by turning a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a detector and finding a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This is the kind of new observational window I value most: a hard instrument-building problem solved, with sources then identified (a flaring blazar, the active galaxy NGC 1068, the Galactic plane).
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit names Halzen alone, as the driving conceiver and leader of IceCube, so a single-laureate prize is possible. The collaboration is large, and AMANDA and the Baikal and ANTARES pioneers also contributed, so the committee must test whether one person's role is decisive enough.
assessment.maturity: Detection was announced in 2013 and has since been followed by multi-messenger source associations and independent consistency checks. The interpretation is stable and recognition looks timely. Individual source evidence is still at moderate significance, but the diffuse flux is firm.
uncertainties: Whether a sole-laureate configuration is fair given the size of the collaboration and the role of earlier detector pioneers.
Independent confirmation of the source associations by other detectors (KM3NeT, Baikal-GVD) is still developing.
I have not independently checked the exact significance figures from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow, followed by optical and radio counterparts and redshift measurements, settled the decades-old gamma-ray burst puzzle and showed that bursts are cosmological. It transformed GRBs into probes of black-hole formation and the distant universe. This sits close to my own interest in gamma-ray bursts and in the instruments used to study them.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX wide-field and narrow-field instrument work that gave arcminute positions and the first X-ray afterglow. Kulkarni led the optical and radio follow-up. Credit is plausible but others (van Paradijs, Groot, Piro, Frail, Djorgovski, Metzger) made decisive contributions, so allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Discovered in 1997 and confirmed repeatedly by Swift and many later missions over nearly three decades. Very mature; if anything, recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among the BeppoSAX team, the optical groups and the radio observers is contested.
Some deserving contributors may not fit within three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea and developed to about 10^-18 fractional uncertainty, are a major precision-measurement advance. They enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear case of a measurement technique opening a new regime, with carefully controlled systematics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock. Ye brought it to the 10^-18 level and widened its use. The two-name configuration looks natural, though Hall and Hänsch (2005) and Wineland (2012) already cover earlier optical frequency metrology and ion clocks, and others such as Lemonde and Pfau contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced and compared lattice clocks at the 10^-18 level, so the confirmation is strong. Recognition is timely, since the redefinition of the second is under discussion.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior frequency-metrology prizes may count against it.
Other groups' contributions to the lattice-clock concept could be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS detectors were extraordinary feats of instrument conception and construction, and they made the 2012 discovery of the Higgs boson possible. The physics importance is unquestionable, though the theory was already recognised in 2013. I would weigh a prize for the experimental method, as in other detector-driven prizes, against the risk of crowding.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee led the proposals and early design, and the first two were project leaders. Many other leaders, including later spokespersons and the accelerator builders, were also decisive. A three-name prize risks omitting people who matter as much, which is a serious difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs discovery has been confirmed and extended by both experiments independently and is fully mature. Timing is acceptable but not pressing, since the theory prize was given in 2013.
uncertainties: Nobel statutes and committee tradition on rewarding large detector collaborations through a few individuals.
Whether this adds enough beyond the 2013 prize.
Fair credit for the many other project leaders and accelerator contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction that neutron-star mergers produce radioactively powered kilonovae, and the discovery of the AT2017gfo counterpart alongside GW170817, confirmed mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis. It is a striking multi-messenger result that fits naturally beside the gravitational-wave prize of 2017.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit is shared by Metzger, Kasen and others, including Li and Paczynski (1998), who are not among the supplied names. Foley is a plausible observational name, but several teams found the counterpart at once (Swope, DECam, Las Cumbres, and others), so the decisive observer is unclear. The credited set is a weak fit for what must be a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: The basis is essentially one well-observed event plus later candidate kilonovae such as GRB 230307A with JWST. The qualitative picture is secure, but the details of r-process yields and ejecta composition are still debated. Recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Missing foundational theory names (Li and Paczynski) cannot be added under this protocol.
Priority among the observing teams is not clear.
Heavy-element yields are still uncertain, and independent events are few.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays found evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries, opening a new band of the gravitational-wave spectrum. It is an ingenious use of the Galaxy as a detector and has enormous scientific value, and the long-term timing is patient detector work.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA). Manchester, Kramer and McLaughlin are leaders of different collaborations, which is reasonable but not exhaustive. Foster, Detweiler, Hellings and Downs and others were involved earlier, and the allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: The 2023 results show the Hellings-Downs correlation at moderate significance (around 2 to 4 sigma by group) and independent PTAs agree, but there is no 5-sigma detection and the source (black-hole binaries versus new physics) is uncertain. This looks premature for now.
uncertainties: Significance is below the usual discovery threshold, so the claim may still change.
Origin of the signal is not established.
Credit across competing collaborations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and of surface Dirac states created a major, long-lasting field of condensed matter physics. It is not my own field, so I would defer to colleagues and expert reviewers on its depth.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the prediction, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang made the HgTe proposal, Molenkamp observed the quantum spin Hall effect, and Hasan did the three-dimensional ARPES work. Among the supplied names I would choose Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan, but that leaves out Mele and a conflict with the Kane/Mele partnership, and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed by many groups, with quantized transport and spectroscopic evidence. Mature, though the Nobel-level practical consequences are still being established.
uncertainties: Overlap with candidate B026 and with the quantum anomalous Hall candidates.
Fairness of leaving out Mele, who is credited in this candidate.
Outside my expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP gave precision measurements of the cosmic microwave background anisotropies and pinned down the age, composition and geometry of the universe, defining the standard cosmological model. It is a landmark of instrument design, with careful treatment of systematics and calibration.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument scientist, and Spergel was a central figure in the cosmological analysis. The CMB has already been recognised in 1978 (discovery), 2006 (COBE) and 2019 (cosmology theory), and the Planck mission and other experiments, plus work by the earlier teams, make credit allocation complicated.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and refined by Planck, ACT and SPT, so strongly mature. Recognition might now seem late and partly overshadowed by Planck and earlier CMB prizes.
uncertainties: Competing credit with COBE, BOOMERanG, Planck and theory contributors.
Possible reluctance to give another CMB prize.
